edits.text: PRELIMINARY STATEMENT. Defendant responds to Plaintiff's First Requests for Production subject to the General Objections and specific responses set forth below. Defendant's responses are based on information presently known and reasonably available after a reasonable inquiry. Defendant reserves all objections, including objections to relevance, proportionality, privilege, work-product protection, confidentiality, undue burden, and admissibility.
edits.name: Preliminary Statement

edits.text: 1. GENERAL OBJECTIONS. Defendant objects to each request to the extent it: (a) seeks information or documents protected by the attorney-client privilege, work-product doctrine, common-interest doctrine, or any other applicable privilege or protection; (b) seeks documents not within Defendant's possession, custody, or control; (c) is overbroad, unduly burdensome, vague, ambiguous, duplicative, or not proportional to the needs of the case; (d) seeks documents that are not relevant to any party's claims or defenses; (e) seeks confidential, proprietary, commercially sensitive, or private information absent an appropriate protective order or confidentiality treatment; or (f) purports to impose obligations beyond those required by the applicable rules, court orders, or governing law. By responding, Defendant does not concede the relevance, discoverability, or admissibility of any requested material, and no response shall be deemed a waiver of any objection or protection.
edits.name: General Objections

edits.text: 2. PRODUCTION. Subject to and without waiving the foregoing objections, Defendant will produce or make available for inspection responsive, non-privileged documents located after a reasonable search and within Defendant's possession, custody, or control. Production will be made in a reasonably usable form, and Defendant is willing to meet and confer regarding ESI search terms, custodians, date ranges, format of production, and any confidentiality designations as appropriate.
edits.name: Production

edits.text: 3. PRIVILEGE LOG. To the extent Defendant withholds responsive documents on the basis of privilege or other protection, Defendant will identify such documents on a privilege log consistent with applicable rules and any agreement or order governing privilege logs. Defendant reserves the right to use categorical logging where appropriate and to withhold privileged communications created after the commencement of this litigation without logging them if permitted by rule, order, or agreement.
edits.name: Privilege Log

edits.text: 4. RESERVATION. Defendant reserves the right to amend, modify, clarify, or supplement these responses and objections as discovery proceeds, as additional information becomes available, and as required by applicable rules or court order. Defendant further reserves the right to object to the use of any produced document on any ground, including relevance, authenticity, hearsay, privilege, confidentiality, and admissibility.
edits.name: Reservation

edits.text: PRELIMINARY STATEMENT. Defendant responds to Plaintiff's First Requests for Production based on information presently known and reasonably available after a reasonable inquiry. Defendant has amended these responses to state the scope of production and, where applicable, whether responsive documents are being withheld on the basis of asserted objections. Defendant will produce responsive, non-privileged documents within its possession, custody, or control after a reasonable and proportional search, subject to the objections and limitations stated below and in the response to each request. Defendant does not waive, and expressly preserves, applicable privileges and protections, including the attorney-client privilege, work-product doctrine, common-interest doctrine, and any confidentiality protections available under governing law or court order.
edits.name: Preliminary Statement - clarified scope and withholding

edits.text: 1. GENERAL OBJECTIONS. Defendant maintains the following general objections to the extent applicable to any request: (a) Defendant objects to producing documents protected by the attorney-client privilege, work-product doctrine, common-interest doctrine, or any other applicable privilege or protection, and will withhold such materials; (b) Defendant objects to producing documents outside its possession, custody, or control and will not search sources it does not control; (c) Defendant objects to requests that are overbroad, unduly burdensome, vague, ambiguous, duplicative, or not proportional to the needs of the case, and will limit its search and production to reasonable, proportional sources and time periods identified in these responses or agreed by the parties; (d) Defendant objects to requests seeking documents not relevant to any party's claims or defenses and will not produce documents solely within irrelevant categories; (e) Defendant objects to producing confidential, proprietary, commercially sensitive, or private information absent appropriate confidentiality treatment, and will designate such materials under any applicable protective order or confidentiality agreement; and (f) Defendant objects to any instruction or definition purporting to impose obligations beyond those required by the applicable rules, court orders, or governing law. Except as expressly stated in a specific response or in this section, Defendant is not withholding responsive, non-privileged documents located after a reasonable search on the basis of general objections alone.
edits.name: General Objections - no boilerplate withholding ambiguity

edits.text: 2. SCOPE OF SEARCH, PRODUCTION, AND ESI. Subject to the objections stated herein, Defendant will conduct a reasonable and proportional search for responsive, non-privileged documents within its possession, custody, or control. Defendant proposes the following ESI protocol, subject to meet-and-confer: (a) custodians: the principal Defendant personnel most likely to possess responsive materials, including relevant decision-makers and personnel directly involved in the events at issue, with final names to be confirmed after the parties confer; (b) date range: the period reasonably tied to the claims and defenses in this action, including a reasonable lead-in and wind-down period, with final dates to be agreed by the parties; (c) search terms: targeted terms directed to the claims, defenses, parties, transaction, communications, and key issues in dispute, to be exchanged and refined cooperatively; (d) sources: reasonably accessible email, electronic documents, shared folders, and hard-copy files likely to contain responsive materials; and (e) format: single-page TIFF images with extracted text/OCR, standard load files, and metadata fields customarily produced in civil litigation, with spreadsheets, databases, audio/video, and other files requiring native format to be produced natively where reasonably necessary. Defendant will produce responsive, non-privileged documents on a rolling basis beginning within 21 days after agreement on search parameters or entry of an appropriate protective order, whichever is later, and will endeavor to complete substantial production within 45 days thereafter, subject to volume, privilege review, third-party confidentiality issues, and any issues identified during collection or review. Defendant will promptly meet and confer if these deadlines require adjustment.
edits.name: Production - custodians/date/search/format/deadline

edits.text: 3. PRIVILEGE LOG. Defendant will withhold documents protected by the attorney-client privilege, work-product doctrine, common-interest doctrine, or other applicable privilege or protection. Defendant will provide a privilege log for responsive documents withheld on those grounds consistent with applicable rules and any protective order, ESI protocol, or stipulation entered in this action. Defendant proposes serving its privilege log within 30 days after substantial completion of document production. Defendant reserves the right to use categorical logging where appropriate, including for email chains, duplicative communications, and privileged communications involving litigation counsel, and proposes that post-complaint communications with litigation counsel need not be logged absent good cause or contrary court order.
edits.name: Privilege log - deadline and scope

edits.text: 4. SPECIFIC REQUEST RESPONSES AND WITHHOLDING STATEMENT. For each specific request, Defendant will state whether it will produce responsive, non-privileged documents, whether it is withholding documents on the basis of privilege or a stated objection, and any limitation on the scope of its search or production. Unless a specific response states otherwise, Defendant will produce responsive, non-privileged documents located after a reasonable search and is not withholding such documents on the basis of objections other than privilege, work-product, confidentiality treatment pending entry of an appropriate protective order, or proportionality limits expressly identified in that response.
edits.name: New specific request withholding statement

edits.text: 5. RESERVATION. Defendant reserves the right to amend, modify, clarify, or supplement these responses and objections as discovery proceeds, as additional information becomes available, and as required by applicable rules or court order. Defendant further reserves the right to object to the use of any produced document on any ground, including relevance, authenticity, hearsay, privilege, confidentiality, and admissibility. Nothing in these responses should be construed as an agreement to search sources, custodians, date ranges, or ESI not reasonably proportional to the needs of the case or not agreed by the parties or ordered by the Court.
edits.name: Renumbered reservation with proportionality qualifier

receiver.message_back: Counsel, Plaintiff appreciates the amendments, but Defendant’s responses remain too open-ended: please provide by Friday the specific custodians, sources, date range, proposed search terms, metadata fields, and any proportionality limits being invoked, and confirm that rolling production will begin within 14 days and will not be delayed wholesale by unresolved disputes over discrete custodians/terms or confidentiality designations. Plaintiff can agree in principle to a reasonable protective order and privilege log 30 days after substantial completion, but we do not agree to categorical logging or exclusion of post-complaint communications absent a stipulated protocol identifying the categories with sufficient detail to test the claim of privilege.
